record.category: managed Postgres and friends with a free plan that powers off on inactivity

free_tier.stated: Free plan with 1 GB RAM and 1 GB total storage per service, on Postgres, MySQL, Valkey, Kafka and OpenSearch; free indefinitely with no time limit, but the service powers off after a period of inactivity

retention.stated: the service powers off after a period of inactivity, on three triggers: no initial usage in the first few hours, or no continuative activity later; a powered-off service is deleted after 180 days. The Free plan is the exception to 'data retention is only limited by storage'

egress.terms: no egress allowance, quota or per-GB rate is published on the free-plan pages or the PostgreSQL pricing table; recorded as a gap after checking both

record.interface_detail: the Postgres wire protocol; an API and the avn CLI
record.tooling: psql and any Postgres client; the avn CLI
record.chaining: no longer a candidate for a weekly or monthly job: the free service powers off on inactivity and is deleted 180 days after it powers off, so a keep-alive is required and the paid Developer tier is what removes the clock

limits.value: 1 GB total storage per service; 1 GB RAM
the free service powers off after a period of inactivity; a service powered off for more than 180 days is automatically deleted
max_connections is set to 20 on a free PostgreSQL service, and there is no connection pooling

identity_cost.detail: email signup; no card on the Free plan

record.reliability_note: free services power off on inactivity and a service powered off for more than 180 days is automatically deleted; a powered-off service for a version past end of life is deleted within 7…
record.confidence_note: three first-party Aiven pages were read on 2026-10-22. The pricing page gives 1 GB RAM and 1 GB storage. The free-PostgreSQL page gives the inactivity power-off. The service power-cycle page gives the 180-day deletion. The pricing page's 'with the exception of Free plan' clause is a carve-out and not boilerplate. The free tier is what it carves out.

evidence.proved: Free column: RAM per VM 1 GB, Total storage 1 GB; Developer USD 5 with 8 GB; Hobbyist from USD 12; 'Data retention is only limited by storage, with the exception of Free plan'

'Service powers off after a period of inactivity (you'll be notified by email and in-platform beforehand)'; 'It's free indefinitely with no time limit, but the service is automatically powered off after a period of inactivity'

two power-off triggers: 'Power off free services with no initial usage within the first few hours after the service is running' and 'Power off free services with no continuative activity on the service'
'Services powered off for more than 180 days are automatically deleted'; the 180-day grace does not apply to an end-of-life version, which is deleted within 7 days
'Developer tier services are not automatically powered off when inactive'; the paid step is what removes the clock
'No connection pooling' and '`max_connections` limit set to `20`' on the free tier

record.notes: 1 GB is the smallest free Postgres storage in this class, and the free plan powers off on inactivity, so it does not answer the question the class was formed to ask. 5 GB is what the plan used to give and several comparison pages still print it. The paid Developer tier at USD 5 a month is the version of this that stays up: 'Developer tier services are not automatically powered off when inactive'.
record.binding_note: 1 GB of storage is small, but the inactivity power-off is what defeats the use a reader would pick this for: an unattended job that runs less often than the inactivity window. The 180-day deletion sets the outer limit.

record.provider: Aiven free tier (PostgreSQL / MySQL / Valkey / OpenSearch / Kafka)

free_tier.stated: 1 GB disk each for PostgreSQL, MySQL and Valkey (Valkey maxmemory = 50% of 1 GB RAM = 512 MB usable); 20 GB storage for OpenSearch; Kafka free tier is throughput-capped at 250 KiB/s. 'Only one service of each service type in your organization.' No time limit, no credit card.

egress.terms: Free. 'Network traffic is not charged separately' (Aiven service pricing doc). This is the best egress term of any structured store here, which makes the tiny byte quotas the only blocker.

record.tooling: psql / mysql / redis-cli / OpenSearch REST API / any Kafka client; Aiven Terraform provider and `avn` CLI for provisioning; PG-wire and RESP protocols unchanged
record.chaining: One service of each type per ORG (verified in the Valkey free-tier doc: 'Only one service of each service type in your organization'). So one org yields ~1 + 1 + 0.5 + 20 GB = ~22.5 GB across four services, plus Kafka. 23 orgs would reach 500 GB. The best per-org yield of any structured store found, and the only one where egress is genuinely free.
record.limits_note: 1 GB disk (PG/MySQL), 1 GB RAM (Valkey, 50% maxmemory), 20 GB + 4 GB RAM + 2 shards (OpenSearch free), Kafka 250 KiB/s ingress/egress with 5 topics x 2 partitions and fixed retention; single node; no VPC; no static IPs; no forking; `max_connections` 20 on free PG
record.reliability_note: Aiven 'reserves the right to power off free services with no initial usage in the first few hours' and to power off services with no continuing activity. For a cold archive that means keep-alive traffic is mandatory or the service sleeps. No data loss reported, just power-off.
